links.title: Hiza-guruma on the IJF technique reference

alt.en: Illustrated sequence of Hiza-guruma, the knee wheel.

image.source: Compiled club reference document supplied by the project owner; original source not recorded

about.en: Tori blocks uke's knee with the sole of the foot and wheels uke forward over it, using rotation of the hands rather than strength.

en: Place the sole lightly on the side of uke's knee, do not kick
Break balance to uke's front corner before the block
Turn the steering-wheel action of the hands all the way through
From a right-handed grip, drift your partner's balance towards their right front corner, drawing them slightly onto their toes.
Step your right foot out to the side, roughly level with their right foot and a shoulder-width away, toes turned out, so your body faces across theirs.
Place the sole of your left foot lightly against the outside of their right knee, at the kneecap. The foot rests there as a block: do not kick or push.
Turn both hands as if turning a large wheel to your left: your left hand pulls their sleeve down past your hip, your right hand carries their lapel up and across.
Their body wheels over the blocked knee. Keep the wheel turning until they roll over and land on their back to your left, and keep the sleeve in your hand.

receiving.en: You feel your balance drawn to your front corner, then a light block arrives at your knee and your body keeps travelling over it. You wheel forwards and land on your back. Your right sleeve is held; tuck your chin, turn with the rotation rather than fighting it, and slap with your left arm as your back lands.

viNotes.en: The block is placed by touch: slide your sole up the outside of their shin until it meets the swell of the knee, then stop pushing and turn your hands. From the gripped-up start the wheel is in the arms in any case, and you can feel it working as soon as their shoulders start turning around a leg that has stopped moving.

cue.en: The sole of the foot blocks the opponent's knee and the hands wheel them forwards over it.
